newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower in quiet trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower in quiet trade as worse-than-expected third quarter earnings and flagging economic growth continued to put a damper on equities.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 0.36 percent to 13,485.38 on a below-average volume of 983.5 million pesos, while Bogota's IBB slipped 0.08 percent to close at 870.89. Volume in Bogota was a thin 670 million pesos.
"Leading shares look like they've fallen asleep and are reflecting the general behavior of the economy," one broker said. "There were no buyers out there today," he added.
The day's biggest loser was Banco Industrial Colombiano, which fell 2.89 percent in Medellin to close at 3,350 pesos per share and 1.42 percent in Bogota, where it ended at 3,450 pesos.
The bank is Colombia's leading wholesaler and an industry leader in asset quality. But brokers said it had been hurt by the 46.6 percent drop in nine-month earnings reported last week.
Cadenalco, Colombia's top retailer in size and sales, also fell on poor earnings. It slipped another 1.11 percent in Wednesday's trade to end at 3,450 pesos a share.
Other losers included Cementos Diamante, a cement manufacturer owned by Mexican cement giant Cementos Mexicanos.

Brokers said Diamante, which closed 2.06 percent lower at 4,231 pesos a share, fell on a cross trade between leading shareholders rather than its own lower-than-expected third quarter earnings, however.
"Foreign funds aren't seeing any interesting share packages and that's part of the reason why the market is so quiet," one broker said.
